values: Cover-page authorization language referencing effluent limitations, monitoring requirements, and conditions in Parts I, II, and III
Permit effective date (January 1, 2022) and expiration (December 31, 2026) stated on the cover page

grounding.excerpt:
This is a reissue, prepared by Maria Okpala, Environmental Engineer, Permitting Section
(6WD-PE), and shall become effective on January 1, 2022

in accordance with this cover page and the effluent limitations, monitoring requirements, and
other conditions set forth in Part I, Part II, and Part III hereof.
This permit and the authorization to discharge shall expire at midnight, December 31, 2026
Packet is auto-assembled from the nominated passage; it may be evidence-insufficient.

rationale: The packet confirms cover-page authorization language tying discharge authority to effluent limitations, monitoring requirements, and conditions in Parts I–III, and confirms the January 1, 2022 effective date and December 31, 2026 expiration. It also labels the permit a reissue. However, the obligation asks whether that reissue characterization requires that limits and monitoring may incorporate unchanged requirements from a superseded permit, or must be determined solely from Parts I–III of this permit. The packet contains no superseded permit, no regulatory reissue-incorporation rule, and no text from Parts I–III. The cover-page cross-reference to Parts I–III does not establish whether those parts merely restate prior requirements or replace them independently. Labeling the document a reissue is not, by itself, establishing evidence that unchanged superseded requirements carry over; nor does it establish that they cannot. Neither the burden for ACCEPT (establishing one branch of the dichotomy) nor REJECT (establishing the other cannot hold) is met. Per P5, unsupported uncertainty is preferred to unsupported semantic closure.
